title: PagerDuty + Slack: Incident Snapshot Assembler and Runbook Suggestion Service
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Build a lightweight service that assembles a concise incident snapshot (traces, top error logs, latency percentile deltas, recent deployments, and sample requests) and attaches it automatically to PagerDuty alerts and the originating Slack incident channel. The service should also surface ranked runbook suggestions and produce a draft postmortem skeleton when an alert meets configured severity/duration thresholds. Goal: reduce MTTI/MTTR by giving oncall engineers a one-click context bundle, suggested remediation steps, and a ready-to-edit postmortem template.

Background: Current incidents rely on engineers to manually gather traces, dashboards, and runbook links. This wastes critical minutes during high-severity incidents and causes inconsistent postmortems. We've already instrumented richer trace hooks and improved metrics/log pipeline coverage; this ticket integrates those signals into an orchestration layer that composes the snapshot.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: PD trigger integration, Slack attachment formatting, snapshot composition (top 3 traces, top 5 error logs, recent deploys, p50/p95/p99 latency deltas, and inferred probable cause tags), runbook recommendation scorer, draft postmortem creation in the postmortem doc store.
- Out-of-scope: automatic remediation actions (rollbacks, autoscaler changes), full natural-language incident summaries (we will include a short heuristically generated summary and plan to iterate).

Technical approach:
1) Snapshot composer microservice subscribes to alert events from the alerting router (alert webhook). It calls internal telemetry APIs: traces-api (to fetch span samples by trace IDs in the alert), logs-search (top error excerpts), metrics-aggregator (latency deltas), and deploys-api (recent deploy metadata).
2) Use lightweight heuristics to rank probable causes: error-class frequency, latency spike localization by service, correlation with recent deploys, and kv-cache-miss percentage. Heuristics are configurable via a policy config.
3) Attach a structured payload to PagerDuty incident via PD V2 Events API (as an attachment/annotation) and post a rich Slack block message in the incident channel with buttons: [Open traces], [Insert runbook], [Create postmortem draft].
4) On postmortem draft creation, prefill template with time windows, signals, probable causes, list of implicated services, and links to traces/PRs for the deploy. Create doc in the postmortem store and return link.

Privacy & security: snapshots may include PII in logs; the service must scrub or redact according to log-redaction policies and respect tenant-specific data retention/KMS boundaries for Private deployments. We will run security review before GA.

Rollout: staged: internal dev team -> subset of enterprise customers (opt-in) -> default for P1/P0 alerts.
acceptance_criteria: When a PagerDuty P0/P1 incident is created in prod, the incident receives a Snapshot attachment within 30s that includes: top 3 traces with links, top 5 error log excerpts (redacted), p50/p95/p99 latency delta, and recent deploy metadata.
Slack incident channel receives a formatted message with action buttons and the PD incident link within 30s of PD creation.
Runbook suggestion API returns a ranked list of candidate runbooks (precision > 0.6 on internal test set) and the top suggestion can be inserted into the Slack thread via the button.

Creating a postmortem draft produces a doc prefilled with timeframe, signals, probable cause tags, implicated services, and links to traces/PRs. Doc link is posted back to Slack and attached to the PD incident.
All log excerpts are redacted per our log-redaction rules and security review signoff is recorded before enabling for customers with Private deployments.
